mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate regimes, or the Fed Funds rate does not exceed 2.5% in any month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE by more than 0.2 percentage points is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-market tightness reduces recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: Across 24 months of monthly UNRATE increases >0.2pp, cumulative 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of no change in UNRATE (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly HOUST index falls by at least 5% from the prior month, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days are negative due to sudden demand shock absorption.
failure_condition: In 10 identified demand shock episodes (HOUST ≥5% drop), 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. pre-shock period).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 3 points is followed by a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower industrial production suggests supply-side easing.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥3 points in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 8 identified supply contraction cycles (INDPRO declines ≥3 two months in a row), 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during baseline supply expansion periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in a month and CPIAUCSL is flat, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 5-day forward return as investors anticipate higher future policy rates and price in rate hike anticipation.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥0.25% and CPIAUCSL does not increase
regime_hint: Neutral inflation and rate hike anticipation
failure_condition: Across 15 such events, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) after controlling for lagged SPX returns and inflation expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS of at least 10,000 jobs for three consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strengthening reduces recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 each month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 12 such labor expansion episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically superior to a baseline of no expansion (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly drop in RSAFS of over 100 million dollars accompanied by a decline in GDPC1 of at least 2% suggests a demand shock; this combination is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >100M and GDPC1 decreases by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: During 7 such demand shock events, 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean p-value > 0.05 across episodes).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for two consecutive months and INDPRO is flat, the S&P 500 shows a positive 20-day forward return as a labor-supply soft landing increases equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3% for two consecutive months and INDPRO is unchanged
failure_condition: In 8 such softening regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive after controlling for lagged SPX and macroeconomic variables (F-test p > 0.05).
